reasons: Both answers state the probe semantics correctly, explain the DB-in-liveness restart loop, and give sound YAML with startupProbe and failureThreshold. B adds useful extras such as timeout tuning, separate alerts and the observation that all capacity was lost, but its rollout advice is muddled and includes a nonexistent kubectl option. A has a small code slip and an overstated claim that healthy pods keep serving during the outage, so the two balance out.

A: Uses @app.get (FastAPI-style) but returns a Flask-style (body, status) tuple, which FastAPI would not treat as a status code
Claims that with the fix healthy pods keep serving during the DB outage, but a dependency-wide outage makes every pod not ready
B: Says restarting pods sit in ContainerCreating; a liveness restart of a container in an existing pod shows CrashLoopBackOff/Running, not ContainerCreating
Suggests 'kubectl rollout pause / --force' to push the new spec; kubectl rollout has no --force and pausing does not apply the new spec
